applyTo: "curriculum/**/*.md,lectures/**/README.md"

# Curriculum and module instructions

- Express modules as learner capabilities and competencies, not as a sequence of product tutorials.
- Preserve the approved 11-unit order and titles unless the Project Owner authorizes a documented change.
- For each module, define purpose, audience/level, prerequisites, measurable learning outcomes, topics, activities, assessments, dependencies, and completion criteria.
- Map learning outcomes to lectures, labs, scenarios, and assessment evidence.
- Avoid duplicating detailed lab procedures in curriculum overview documents; link to the canonical module assets.
- Keep Digital Forensics, Memory Forensics, Active Directory, and Vulnerability Management outside the current core scope unless formally approved.
- Use consistent terminology and identify assumptions or unresolved decisions explicitly.


## Bilingual authoring requirements

- Arabic and English are first-class project languages. Follow `governance/policies/bilingual-content-policy.md`.
- Keep paired documents in the same directory; English uses the canonical filename and Arabic appends `-ar` before the extension.
- Preserve stable IDs, technical meaning, commands, code, SPL, field names, configuration keys, numeric values, safety boundaries, evidence, and assessment requirements.
- Update both language variants together when meaning changes, or mark the counterpart `needs-update`/pending. Do not claim parity without reviewing both.
